properties.name: Sierra de la Madera (eastern slopes)
properties.reasoning: Sierra La Madera is the Sky Island range in the municipios of Cumpas, Granados, Huásabas, Moctezuma and Villa Hidalgo (Bermudez-Enriquez et al. 2013, USDA RMRS-P-67). GeoNames 9028461 lies between those towns: 27 km east of Cumpas and 21 km west of Huásabas on the Bavispe (pipeline/measure/distances.py). The book puts the wolf on its eastern slopes, then across the Bavispe and north, which fits a range bounded on the east by the river. GeoNames 3996948, a closer name match, lies east of the river's upper course and would need no crossing.

properties.name: Crossing of the Bavispe
properties.reasoning: The book names no crossing point. The Bavispe runs along the eastern foot of the Sierra La Madera past Granados, Huásabas and Villa Hidalgo, so a wolf leaving the eastern slopes crosses it there. The circle is centred on that reach and reaches Granados and Villa Hidalgo (16.6 km each way).

properties.name: The border at 108°30′ W
properties.reasoning: The book gives this exactly. West of 108°12′ W the boundary follows the parallel 31°20′ N (Gadsden Purchase, 1853), so the point is 31.33333 N, 108.5 W.

properties.name: Whitewater Creek
properties.reasoning: GNIS 896564: the only Whitewater Creek between the border point and the San Luis Mountains.

properties.name: Animas Valley
properties.reasoning: The GNIS pin for the valley is 108 km north, at 32.57 N. The stop is where her route from the Animas Mountains to the Peloncillos crosses the valley floor.

properties.name: Foster Draw (the calf)
properties.reasoning: GNIS 889164 in Hidalgo County; the other two Foster Draws are 158 km and 284 km away.

properties.name: Skeleton Creek, south fork
properties.reasoning: GNIS has no Skeleton Creek here; Skeleton Canyon (GNIS 11397) carries its south fork in Cochise County.

properties.name: Starvation Canyon
properties.reasoning: GNIS 11797, Cochise County, 6 km from Skeleton Canyon.

properties.name: Hog Canyon Springs
properties.reasoning: GNIS 5857, Cochise County, 9 km from Starvation Canyon.

properties.name: Between Clanton and Foster draws
properties.reasoning: The high country between Clanton Draw (GNIS 887634) and Foster Draw (GNIS 889164), which lie 3 km apart.

properties.name: Robertson's crossfence
properties.reasoning: Between the Cloverdale Creek road and the Guadalupe pass. The Robertson family ran the Cloverdale Ranch from the early 1900s (Range Magazine, winter 2000, rangemagazine.com/archives/stories/winter00/bootheel.htm), so the fence is likely theirs. GNIS has no Robertson ranch and the ranch's bounds are not known here; the circle covers the ground between the road and the pass.

properties.name: Low pass in the easternmost Guadalupes
properties.reasoning: The east flank of the Guadalupe Mountains (GNIS 920606), where a pass would lead south-west toward the boundary.

properties.name: Ranch house on the volcanic plain
properties.reasoning: Past the Guadalupe pass and before the boundary. The book crosses a broad volcanic plain here. The Geronimo–San Bernardino volcanic field covers the northern San Bernardino Valley in basalt, from Cochise County into Hidalgo County and Sonora (New Mexico Geological Society guidebook; Arizona Geological Survey), which is the ground south-west of the pass. The ranch house itself is unnamed.

properties.name: The boundary, a monument in sight
properties.reasoning: Boundary monuments stand along 31°20′ N here. The circle covers the stretch south of the volcanic plain and north of the Cajon Bonita.

properties.name: Down the Cajon Bonita
properties.reasoning: The book spells it Cajon Bonita. GeoNames 4016262, the Cajón Bonito nearest the boundary; the other two are 89 km and 122 km away.

properties.name: The mud-house settlement
properties.reasoning: Unnamed. Between the crossing at Colonia Oaxaca and Colonia Morelos.

properties.name: Into the Pilares Teras
properties.reasoning: GeoNames 3981872, Sierra de Teras, which GeoNames also lists as Pilares de Teras.

properties.reasoning: They pass Colonia Morelos after midnight.

properties.name: Bacerac (Keno)

The book's compass does not close here: the brothers then ride south into pinewoods and reach Las Varas, which lies to the north, two days later. The circle is wide for that reason.

properties.name: Las Varas
properties.reasoning: Two days without food, they cross the railroad tracks into Las Varas, pass the maize warehouses and the station, and eat at a café.

properties.name: Quijada's remuda

The book gives no distances; the circle is north-east of the tracking camp.

properties.name: Boquilla y Anexas (the manco falls)
properties.reasoning: After a night at a stone tank with a windmill on the high prairie (3-05), they ride into Boquilla y Anexas at noon and buy rope; in the alameda the manco's horse falls back on him (3-07).

properties.reasoning: About a mile above the town they turn off the road and head west to a river with nine horses, turning the Boquilla horses back. The book does not name the river; the circle is north-west of La Boquilla.

properties.reasoning: They cross the river upcountry, ride all night through open country away from it, and make a dry camp toward morning in a burned grove on a rise a mile west of the river. The circle is between Boquilla and San José, which are 48 km apart (bearing 340 degrees).

properties.reasoning: Next morning they head north, cross the river, find no road and follow the river north to the pueblito of San José, where a woman feeds them. The pick is a best fit (see the place's reasoning and docs/open-questions.md).

properties.name: The blind man's house
properties.reasoning: Alone, Billy leads his horse up an arroyo, sees a light far to the north at dusk and goes toward it; near midnight he reaches a fence, turns east to a gate and rides up a clay track to a lone house, where the blind man and his wife take him in. The circle is north of the shooting, about a day and a half south of Mata Ortiz by the text's timing.

properties.name: The desert crossroads on the main road north
properties.reasoning: Next morning he rides north along the road and before noon strikes the main road north to Casas Grandes at an empty desert crossroads; he sleeps in a field near the river breaks and rides on in rain. The circle is on the road south of Mata Ortiz.

properties.name: Mata Ortiz, the blue tienda
properties.reasoning: In the evening he crosses the railroad into Mata Ortiz, where the woman at a small blue tienda tells him his brother passed alive in the truck.

properties.name: San Diego, where he finds Boyd

properties.name: Casas Grandes at 3 a.m., for the doctor

properties.name: Back to San Diego, in the doctor's car
properties.reasoning: He rides back with the doctor in the doctor's old Dodge, south on the road and up the ejido road over the wooden bridge; the doctor treats Boyd and leaves at dawn.

properties.name: San Diego, leaving at dusk
properties.reasoning: Billy leaves the ejido at dusk to meet the girl at Santa Ana de Babícora, as Boyd asks, and takes the road south, under the cottonwoods by the river.

properties.name: Mata Ortiz
properties.reasoning: He passes through Mata Ortiz the first night and sleeps in a grove off the road.

properties.reasoning: He rides all day, meets the workers' truck in the evening, and in the night hears a train whistle for the crossing at Las Varas. The circle is north-east of Las Varas, on the way to Boquilla.

properties.name: Boquilla at noon
properties.reasoning: He reaches Boquilla at noon and takes the road south toward Santa Ana de Babícora.

properties.name: La Pinta by moonlight
properties.reasoning: He passes La Pinta under the moon; it sits on a high plain of juniper over the Santa María valley.

properties.name: Santa Ana de Babícora at midnight
properties.reasoning: He waters his horse in the alameda at midnight and takes the road west toward Namiquipa.

properties.name: A stream of the Santa María headwaters
properties.reasoning: An hour along the road west he sleeps beside a stream, one of the Santa María's headwaters, and in the morning the girl rides past on his mother's old horse. properties.name: Back through Santa Ana, with the girl
properties.reasoning: They ride back through Santa Ana near noon and eat in a grove north of the town, passing three girls on their way to Soto Máynez.

properties.name: La Boquilla after dark
properties.reasoning: They reach La Boquilla after dark and pass the place where the manco fell.

properties.reasoning: They ride on west into the dark and camp at the edge of the lake. The circle is on the north-west shore of the Babícora lake (GeoNames 4017246), on the way to Las Varas.

properties.name: Las Varas
properties.reasoning: At noon they cross the wooden river bridge into Las Varas and meet the opera company's arriero, who tells what became of the troupe.

properties.name: Camp on the river south of Mata Ortiz
properties.reasoning: They take the road north by the railroad; the ride to San Diego takes three days, and the last night they stop for the night on a gravel bar by the river, several miles below Mata Ortiz, as cranes pass over heading south. properties.name: San Diego, on a feast day
properties.reasoning: They cross the plank bridge to the hacienda at noon on a feast day.

properties.name: Cuauhtémoc, as far south as he rides
properties.reasoning: Boyd and the girl are gone. Billy looks for them for weeks, riding as far south as Cuauhtémoc. The book gives the turning points of the search, not its roads.

properties.name: Namiquipa
properties.reasoning: He rides north again to Namiquipa, where no one owns to knowing the girl.

properties.name: La Norteña, as far west as he rides
properties.reasoning: His westernmost point is La Norteña and the watershed.

properties.name: The crossroads at Buenaventura
properties.reasoning: At dawn he sits his horse at the crossroads in Buenaventura, watching waterfowl over the river and the lagunas.

properties.name: Galeana
properties.reasoning: He passes back north through Galeana.

properties.reasoning: In the early days of December, two days without food, he reaches Casas Grandes past midnight in a cold rain and learns that the doctor is dead. Part III ends here; Part IV opens at the Columbus gate, and the book does not tell the ride north.

properties.reasoning: Reported by the singer, a girl shelling pecans at the Camino Recto hotel in Casas Grandes (4-05): in her corrido six armed riders come to the pueblo of Bachíniva in April, and the güerito and his sweetheart die together there. Quijada's account, the next stops, differs.

properties.name: Galeana, two men killed

properties.name: San Buenaventura, the grave

properties.name: The border at Columbus

properties.name: Back to Deming

properties.name: Albuquerque, rejected again

properties.name: Deming at three in the morning
properties.reasoning: He is on the bus south before noon and reaches Deming at three in the morning; the book names no place on the way back, so the line is a curve.

properties.name: Hachita, leaving the road

properties.name: The Little Hatchet foothills
properties.reasoning: His way runs across the lower slopes of the Little Hatchet Mountains and over the railroad from the Phelps Dodge smelter.

properties.reasoning: In the morning they cross the lake, strike the old Playas road before noon and follow it west into the mountains, with snow in the pass. The book does not name the pass; the circle is in the Animas Mountains west of the lake.

properties.name: Animas
properties.reasoning: He rides down into the Animas Valley and takes the road south from Animas.

properties.name: Camp on the Animas Plain
properties.reasoning: That night's camp is out on the wide Animas Plain, with lightning showing in the far south past the Hatchet Mountains. The circle is on the open plain south-east of the Sanders estimate.

properties.name: Winslow, paid off from the Hashknife linecamp
properties.reasoning: Told in summary: he works for the Hashknives at a linecamp on the Little Colorado, and when paid in March goes into the town the book calls Window (Winslow) to the post office and the bars on First Street. properties.name: Magdalena
properties.reasoning: Nine months on, he heads south over the high plains on the west side of Socorro and passes through Magdalena.

properties.name: The plains of San Agustín
properties.reasoning: He crosses the plains the book calls Saint Augustine, riding south.

properties.name: Silver City, Christmas
properties.reasoning: He reaches Silver City in snow, takes a room at the Palace Hotel and finds it is Christmas Day.

properties.name: A small ranch out of Magdalena
properties.reasoning: Told in summary: he drifts to the Texas panhandle (the Matadors, the T Diamond; outside the map) and back, and in the spring of the war's third year has work on a little ranch near Magdalena until March. The pin is the town.

properties.name: East of Steins, the last blacktop
properties.reasoning: Heading south with a packhorse, he crosses the last paved highway he will meet, a short way east of Steins.

properties.name: The SK Bar gate
properties.reasoning: Two days later he reaches the SK Bar gate, learns that Miller died on Kwajalein, and stays the night in the rain. The circle is the J3 estimate (docs/open-questions.md).

properties.name: Mexican customs at Berendo
properties.reasoning: He signs the horses through Mexican customs at Berendo (El Berrendo, opposite Antelope Wells) and rides south. The book does not tell the ride from the SK Bar to the gate.

properties.name: Janos
properties.reasoning: After two days' riding on an old rutted wagon road, with the western Sierras and the Pilares in view, he comes down to the lights of Janos, 59 km from El Berrendo (pyproj, WGS 84).

properties.name: Casas Grandes
properties.reasoning: He rides south all day and passes through Casas Grandes in the evening.

properties.name: San Diego, the families gone
properties.reasoning: He takes the road south he rode with Boyd past the ruins, and at San Diego finds the Muñoz house empty.

properties.name: Las Varas
properties.reasoning: Two days later he passes Las Varas and turns east toward La Boquilla.

properties.name: Camp on the plain by the lake, the red plane
properties.reasoning: On the road east toward La Boquilla a north wind blows dust off Babícora beyond the lake, a red plane flies in from the west, and he camps on the plain. The circle is north-east of the Babícora lake.

properties.name: Babícora
properties.reasoning: Next day he rides through Babícora. The pin is the Hacienda de San José de Babícora, the Hearst ranch headquarters (see the place's reasoning).

properties.name: Santa Ana de Babícora
properties.reasoning: He rides through Santa Ana de Babícora and takes the road north to Namiquipa.

properties.name: Namiquipa, now a mining camp
properties.reasoning: He camps below the town in the river willows. At a wake (4-05) a woman tells him the girl is hunted and that his brother's bones lie at San Buenaventura.

properties.name: Temósachic
properties.reasoning: He rides that country for weeks asking after the girl; the first time he hears the corrido of the güero is in a bodega in Temósachic, up in the mountains.

properties.name: Madera, the late April fair
properties.reasoning: In late April he walks through a fair beyond the railtracks at Madera and sees the opera company's old caravan, then leaves Madera on the southbound road for Temósachic.

properties.name: Babícora before dawn
properties.reasoning: A week later he rides through Babícora again in the early-morning dark and follows the freshly graded road north, sleeping at a ciénega.

properties.name: Casas Grandes, the Camino Recto hotel
properties.reasoning: On 15 May he takes a room at the Camino Recto hotel, where a girl shelling pecans sings him the corrido of Bachíniva. The book gives no distance from Babícora.

properties.name: The high country of the Babícora
properties.reasoning: For days he camps in the swales of the Babícora high country and watches vaqueros working whiteface cattle on mules. The circle covers the plains around the lake and the ranch headquarters.

properties.name: Quijada's cabin
properties.reasoning: One evening he follows a road west toward a gap in the mountains and after dark reaches a lone weatherboard cabin on the plain, where Quijada, still manager of the Nahuerichic division, tells him where Boyd fell and lies. Next day he rides north all day to San Buenaventura, so the circle is about a day's ride (47 km) south-south-west of it. It is 57 km from Nahuerachi, the open-questions pick for the division's name.

properties.name: San Buenaventura
properties.reasoning: He rides north all day in rain and enters San Buenaventura in the evening, past the alameda and the church.

properties.name: Boyd's grave, on the Gallego road
properties.reasoning: The cemetery is on a bench in the low hills east of town, a mile or so up the old road to Gallego, with the Sierra del Nido in sight. He finds the board cross by the south wall and digs all day. The circle is centred 1.6 km due east of the town point.

properties.name: Past the lights of Casas Grandes, to the west
properties.reasoning: Near midnight he leaves with the bones on the packhorse, crosses the highway and heads across country with the polestar to his right. In two nights' riding he sees the lights of Casas Grandes to the west of him, so he is east of the town; the circle is 15 km east of it.

properties.name: The Casas Grandes River, across the Guzmán road
properties.reasoning: He crosses the old road that runs down from Guzmán and Sabinal, reaches the Casas Grandes River and follows a trail north beside it. The circle is on the river south of Corralitos.

properties.name: Corralitos before dawn
properties.reasoning: He passes through the half-ruined town before full light, past slagheaps, and crosses the railroad tracks.

properties.name: The attack on the river trail, and the gypsies' camp
properties.reasoning: An hour north of the town four riders stop him on the trail, cut open the bones and stab Niño; the next day gypsies hauling an old airplane north camp with him by the river and doctor the horse (4-06, 4-07). An hour's ride is about 6 km; the circle is centred 5.8 km north of Corralitos.

properties.name: The border, west of Dog Springs
properties.reasoning: Four days later he sets out north along the river with the bones on a travois; it takes three days to reach the border, where he passes the first boundary obelisk west of Dog Springs and an old dry reservoir. No Dog Springs is known on the line (docs/open-questions.md); the circle is the best estimate, the boundary south of Hermanas.

properties.name: Hermanas
properties.reasoning: Next day he rides through Hermanas and along the dusty road west.

properties.name: Hachita, the crossroads store
properties.reasoning: That evening he sits his horse at the crossroads by the store in Hachita, the book's Hatchita, and looks south-west to the Animas Peaks.

properties.name: Animas, Ash Wednesday
properties.reasoning: He crosses the Animas Valley all day with the travois and reaches Animas next morning, which the book calls Ash Wednesday.

properties.name: The little cemetery south of Animas
properties.reasoning: He buys a spade and goes south from the town to a little cemetery, where he buries Boyd; the sheriff tells him to report at Lordsburg. GNIS lists no cemetery here; the circle is just south of the town.

properties.name: Silver City
properties.reasoning: He rides north to Silver City.

properties.name: Duncan, Arizona
properties.reasoning: He rides west to Duncan.

properties.name: Glenwood
properties.reasoning: He rides north through the mountains to Glenwood.

properties.name: Reserve
properties.reasoning: He rides on to Reserve. He works for the Carrizozos and the GS outfits; the book tells this in summary and the ranches have no point.

properties.name: Silver City, July
properties.reasoning: In July he drifts south to Silver City again. The months between are told in summary.

properties.name: The Santa Rita mines
properties.reasoning: His route east is the old road by the Santa Rita mines.

properties.name: San Lorenzo, New Mexico
properties.reasoning: He rides through San Lorenzo on the old road east.

properties.name: Over the Black Range
properties.reasoning: He crosses the Black Range on the old road east. The book names no pass; the road from San Lorenzo crosses the range at Emory Pass (GNIS 906157), where the circle is centred.

properties.name: The ruined waystation by the blacktop
properties.reasoning: Beyond the range he crosses a plain of catclaw and creosote, strikes the blacktop a few miles on, sees the Organ Mountains about eighty miles off, and turns back along the highway to three ruined adobes with a rusted gas pump, once a waystation. There he drives off the crippled dog, and wakes to the false dawn (4-09). The circle is on the plain east of Hillsboro; its centre is 112 km (70 miles) straight-line from the Organ Mountains point (GNIS 920657, pyproj, WGS 84), and Emory Pass is 131 km (81 miles), so the book's eighty miles fits the range's eastern foot.
